```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(gridpin)
sheet <- system.file("extdata", "tiny.bin", package = "gridpin")
```

## When the address is ambiguous

An address without a town can match the same street in several places. With `k` greater than
one, `gp_geocode()` returns a long table: one row per candidate, numbered by `rank`.

```{r}
gp_geocode("1 Main Street", sheet, k = 3)[, c("query", "rank", "commune", "precision", "weak")]
```

With `k = 1` (the default) you get the best candidate only, one row per address. The best
candidate of a `k = 3` call is not always the same as the single answer of a `k = 1` call:
keep `k = 1` when you want one answer per address, and use `k > 1` to show alternatives to a
person who chooses.

## From coordinates to the nearest address

```{r}
gp_reverse(c(40.7504, 40.7601), c(-73.9904, -73.9801), sheet)[,
  c("point", "housenumber", "street", "distance_m")]
```

Streets without house points are indexed by their centre, so the nearest answer can be some
distance away: `distance_m` says how far. Missing coordinates (`NA`) give a row without an
answer.

## Opening and closing

`gp_open()` maps the file into memory once; later calls with the same file reuse it, and several
R sessions share the pages. `gp_close()` releases it.

```{r}
g <- gp_open(sheet)
g
gp_close(g)
```
